Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-13
Start: 11:00 AM PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood SE), Evan (Oxley CTO), Rina (Oxley SRE), Tom (Oxley Security), Liam (Platform)

Summary:
- Oxley is evaluating Redwood for private deployment (VPC/on-prem options) with an immediate goal to move from sandbox to production within 8-10 weeks.
- Primary concerns: region gating, private endpoints vs peering, egress IPs, KMS integration and audit logs.
- Agreed to a hands-on pilot + network config exchange and security docs.

Topics covered:
- Topology options: VPC Peering, Transit Gateway, PrivateLink/Private Endpoints
- Regional restrictions for data residency and blocked regions list
- Egress and NAT IP planning for allowlists
- KMS + HSM options and key ownership
- Demo/test plan: sandbox->prod cutover checklist and pilot SLOs

Action items recap (see action_items field for owners/dates)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: ok hello everyone thanks for taking the time this morning um i'm jordan from redwood also have priya and maya from our se team hi all
[00:08] Evan: hey thanks, appreciate you fitting us in, we've been triaging this with platform and security, lots to run through
[00:13] Priya: quick agenda — topo options, what oxley's current network looks like, blockers, and then we can sketch a pilot. sound good?
[00:20] Rina: yeah, that'll work. high level — we run prod in us-west-2 and staging in eu-west-1, we have a compliance requirement that certain workloads cannot leave eu-west-1 for data residency reasons
[00:33] Tom: and security wants KMS keys to be customer-managed. we can't hand keys to third parties. also need audit logs available for 1 year on request
[00:42] Maya: totally understood. Redwood supports customer KMS and HSM integrations for Private deployments; we've done per-tenant key policies. for hosted we can integrate but customers often prefer Private for full key ownership
[00:55] Liam: small ask — we need predictable egress IPs for our downstream partners so allowlist can be static, can you do that with private endpoints?
[01:04] Priya: yes — in Dedicated/Private setups you can allocate NAT or egress IPs behind a transit gateway or egress tier. for hosted multi-tenant that's harder, but private deployment gives static egress blocks
[01:18] Evan: what about peering vs private endpoints? which do you recommend for us?
[01:22] Jordan: good question. peering is simpler for intra-account low-latency traffic, but it doesn't scale well across many VPCs or cross-account routing. PrivateLink/private endpoints (cloud provider specific) or a Transit Gateway approach gives centralization and controlled egress. depends on your scale and need for central inspection
[01:36] Rina: we have ~10 VPCs across prod and staging and two on-prem datacenters that will need access. we want a single connectivity pattern for auditors to review
[01:45] Priya: so transit gateway + PrivateLink fronting Redwood would be a common pattern — traffic flows via TGW peering/attachments, and we expose private endpoints into the customer's VPCs so you keep control of egress and routing policies
[01:58] Tom: is there any backchannel to redwood's control plane? i.e., does any traffic cross public internet?
[02:03] Maya: for Private deployments the control plane can be customer-managed in a VPC — so there is no public egress. In hosted mode, control-plane calls may traverse managed infrastructure but data plane paths can be restricted with private endpoints in some setups. we should map this for your exact topology
[02:22] Evan: ok, KMS: would redwood hold key material in hosted? what's the recommendation for us given strict controls?
[02:29] Jordan: if you need customer solely-managed keys, Private deployment with customer KMS/HSM is the recommended path. we support both symmetric keys via cloud KMS and HSM-backed keys for FIPS-level requirements
[02:42] Rina: audit logs — can we ship raw logs to our S3 bucket and keep them for 1 year? we want tamper-evident storage
[02:49] Priya: yes — Private can push audit logs to your logging endpoints, S3 or an on-prem collector. we also support syslog forwarding and can sign logs if required as part of the compliance workflow
[03:03] Liam: about region restrictions — we need to ensure no inference traffic routes through certain countries, can that be enforced at the routing layer?
[03:11] Maya: routing policy + region gating in our orchestration layer can prevent model placement in disallowed regions. operationally we pin model workers to allowed regions and add health checks and automated fallback only to permitted zones
[03:26] Tom: what about latency — our SLA to customers is 200ms p95 for small context prompts, how do you guarantee that across private setups?
[03:34] Priya: latency depends on physical proximity of workers and your VPC egress path; for P95 200ms we typically recommend edge deployment in the same cloud region as the client or a dedicated capacity pool in us-west-2 with direct routing. we'll provide benchmark runs during pilot
[03:48] Evan: can we do a pilot in our staging eu-west-1 region first?
[03:52] Jordan: absolutely. pilot plan: deploy a Private instance in eu-west-1, connect via PrivateLink to your staging VPC, run synthetic latency + throughput tests, and validate KMS integration and log streaming
[04:02] Rina: good. what credentials and artifacts do you need from us to start?
[04:06] Priya: we'll need VPC CIDRs, a list of subnets for endpoints, route table attachments, a short list of IPs that must be allowed outbound to your partners, and the KMS key ARN if you're providing it. for transit gateway pattern we'll need the TGW id and attachment accounts
[04:21] Evan: i'll get that. security will review request for key policy sharing.
[04:26] Tom: incident response — do you provide runbooks and SLA windows for failover?
[04:31] Maya: yes — we provide runbooks, can configure automatic model fallback to a lower-capacity region, and offer outage playbooks. for Dedicated/Private we support 99.9% uptime SLA options as add-ons
[04:45] Liam: note on IP planning: our downstream partner in eu-west-1 only allows three CIDR blocks, we need to know how many egress IPs you'll require during bursts
[04:55] Priya: we'll estimate based on token rates and concurrency — for the pilot we'll provide a conservative number, then refine after test runs. you can also configure autoscaling with fixed egress pools to keep allowlist stable
[05:10] Evan: are there any special firewall/proxy requirements? we run an outbound proxy for all services
[05:16] Jordan: that's fine — as long as proxies allow the private endpoint IPs or you place Redwood endpoints within the same VPC and route via TGW. for proxies we sometimes need to exchange TLS cert pins if deep inspection is performed
[05:30] Tom: about SSO and RBAC — we use SAML + SCIM, will Redwood integrate?
[05:34] Maya: yes, we do SSO SAML and SCIM provisioning for Private and Hosted. for Private deployments you can also integrate with on-prem AD through SAML or LDAP bridges. role mapping and audit hooks are available
[05:48] Rina: any known gotchas we should watch for during sandbox->prod cutover?
[05:52] Priya: two common ones — CIDR overlap during peering, and hardcoded IPs in downstream services. we recommend a network readiness check and an allowlist freeze for the cutover window. also key rotation strategy should be tested in staging
[06:08] Evan: timeline — we want production in ~8-10 weeks, what's realistic?
[06:12] Jordan: with an existing TGW and VPCs we can often do pilot in 2-3 weeks, then a 4-6 week production rollout depending on approvals and compliance review. so 8-10 weeks is achievable if the key stakeholders sign off quickly
[06:26] Liam: pricing — does private deployment have a one-time setup fee and ongoing infra cost?
[06:30] Jordan: yes, Private has an onboarding fee for the private control plane and per-capacity pricing (reserved + autoscale). we'll send a pricing sketch post-call once we know expected concurrent capacity
[06:40] Tom: competitors — we've also looked at vendor x and cloud native private endpoints from aws; what differentiates redwood for us?
[06:46] Maya: main differentiators: unified control plane across hosted/dedicated/private, higher-throughput serving runtime optimized for batching, and operational observability for token-level cost/latency. plus we provide flexible key integrations and audit hooks out of the box
[06:59] Evan: ok that helps, let's talk required artifacts — i'll have a network engineer share CIDRs and TGW details by monday
[07:06] Jordan: perfect. we'll compile the security pack and a network template and follow up with an invite for the lab.
[07:12] Rina: one more question — data residency proof for auditors, do you provide signed attestations?
[07:18] Priya: we can provide compliance artifacts and signed statements as part of the enterprise compliance pack; for Private we can also provide architecture diagrams with pinned regions to present to auditors
[07:30] Tom: great. any other blockers?
[07:33] Evan: none from me. thanks everyone.
[07:36] Jordan: thanks all. recap in the follow-up: network template, SOC/KMS docs, schedule lab, oxley sends CIDRs and TGW, redwood drafts pilot plan. we'll target the lab the week of 8/24
[07:50] call ends
